pairs.subject: trust-base
pairs.evidence: e2e/guide.spec.ts:16 JSON.parse returns TypeScript's unchecked `any` into an unannotated binding whose members (`data["@type"]`, `data.numberOfItems`, `data.description`) are read on lines 17-19. That makes it a trust-base member with nothing at the call site to spell it. The repo's lint setup has no type-aware unsafe-any rule (eslint.config.mjs extends only nextVitals/nextTs, with no projectService and no no-unsafe-* rules), so no census would count it. The practical harm is small, because each read goes straight into a runtime `expect`.

techniques.evidence: e2e/guide.spec.ts:16 The technique's 'unchecked type is a value' case: a standard decoder returns `any` with no directive or `as` to count. It is neither decoded into `unknown` and checked (the removal the technique ranks first) nor counted by a type-aware lint. A grep of the 12 context specs for JSON.parse, `as any`, `: any`, @ts- and .json() found only this site.

e2e/review-undo.spec.ts:75 The only spelled assertion in the context is a double cast whose claimed shape is optional and is written by the same evaluate callback (line 79). It does not rest on a distant declaration, so there is no dependency edge to name at two ends.
